answer: An agent economy blunts Sybil attacks with stake-backed identity: a public identity atlas maps each participant to one key plus a locked collateral bond, keeping power at one identity, one vote. The velvet rope is that bond every fake persona needs fresh collateral, and double-voting or collusion gets it slashed. Influence never grows with clones, while cost rises linearly: each extra Sybil adds a delta to the attacker's bill but no extra sway. A thousand forged agents demand a thousand bonds, burning capital for zero control, so the attack is economically irrational.
